answer: Operator Liability Escrow links every agent identity to a named human or firm whose own assets sit behind it. When a gale of new identities from one operator triggers correlated fraud, the escrow seizes that operator's shared collateral across all their identities at once. Attackers must therefore fund real, seizable capital per operator, not per wallet, and a single flagged cluster can spiral into total loss of that collateral. Honest operators earn a nectar of reduced escrow requirements over time, while the cost of a mass identity farm becomes the full operator bond.
